keyVerseText: These are the families of the Zebulunites according to those that were numbered of them, threescore thousand and five hundred.
rootMeaning: The term זְבוּלֹנִי (Zebulonite) is patronymically derived from זְבוּלוּן (Zebulun), which means 'exalted.' Zebulun was the tenth son of Jacob and the progenitor of the tribe bearing his name. Thus, the root meaning conveys not just a tribal affiliation but also a sense of honor or exaltation inherent in the name Zebulun, which enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing a distinguished lineage within Israel.
usageInScripture: The word זְבוּלֹנִי appears three times in Scripture, consistently referring to a member or descendant of the tribe of Zebulun. It is translated variously as 'of the Zebulunites,' 'a Zebulonite,' or 'the Zebulonite,' reflecting both individual and collective identity. This consistency in usage highlights the word's role in identifying tribal heritage and belonging within the broader narrative of Israel's families.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding זְבוּלֹנִי as rooted in 'exalted' reminds believers that God's covenant people are chosen and honored through their lineage and His promises. The tribe of Zebulun, as part of Israel, signifies God's faithfulness in preserving His people and fulfilling His purposes through distinct families. For the Christian faith, this underscores the continuity of God's redemptive plan beginning with the patriarchs and extending to the community of believers, who are spiritually grafted into this heritage of exaltation through Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 26:27 enumerates the families of the Zebulunites, stating the number of those counted as sixty-five thousand five hundred. The use of זְבוּלֹנִי here emphasizes the collective identity and strength of this tribe within Israel. It highlights God's providential care in organizing and blessing His people, showing that each member, as a Zebulonite, is part of a larger, exalted community under His sovereign counting and care.
